s1.title: Introduction
s1.body: This Privacy Policy describes how FondoRetiro DeFi (hereinafter, 'the Protocol') handles information from users who interact with the smart contracts deployed on the public blockchain. By using the Protocol, you acknowledge that you have read, understood, and accepted the terms set forth herein.

s2.title: Information Recorded on Blockchain
s2.b2: Amounts deposited, withdrawn, and transferred (in USDC or other configured ERC-20 tokens).
s2.b3: Address of the personal fund created through PersonalFundFactory.
s2.b4: Fund parameters: declared age, retirement age, monthly deposit, initial capital, selected DeFi protocol, and timelock period.
s2.b5: Selected investment protocol (MockAaveAdapter, MockOndoAdapter, or others registered in ProtocolRegistry).
s2.b6: User preference settings in UserPreferences (strategy, risk tolerance, autocompounding).
s2.b8: Emitted events: FundCreated, Deposited, Withdrawn, UserConfigUpdated, DepositRouted, among others.

s3.title: Information We Do NOT Collect
s3.b1: Name, surname, identity document, or personally identifiable data outside the blockchain.
s3.b2: Physical address, email, phone number, or contact details.
s3.b3: Biometric or financial information outside blockchain operations.
s3.b4: Cookies, device identifiers, or web browsing/session data.

s4.title: Public Nature of Data
s4.body: Every transaction on a public blockchain is, by nature, public, permanent, and immutable. Anyone can consult the transaction history of a wallet address through block explorers. The Protocol cannot delete, modify, or hide information already recorded.

s5.title: Use of Information
s5.b1: Calculate and execute deposits, withdrawals, and yield distribution.
s5.b2: Verify timelock conditions and withdrawal eligibility.
s5.b3: Route deposits to selected DeFi protocols via UserPreferences.
s5.b4: Record the history of contributions to the retirement fund.

s6.title: Third-Party Data
s6.body: The Protocol interacts with third-party DeFi protocols (Aave v3, Ondo USDY) whose own privacy policies apply independently. Review those policies before selecting a protocol.

s7.title: Security
s7.body: The Protocol's security is based on the immutability of smart contracts and access controls through administrator roles and authorized contracts. The user is solely responsible for the security of their private key.

s8.title: User Rights
s8.b1: Freely access all public information about their fund through any block explorer.
s8.b2: Revoke access of authorized contracts through revokeContract in UserPreferences.
s8.b3: Select and modify their investment protocol and strategy, subject to timelock conditions.

s9.title: Changes to this Policy
s9.body: This Policy may be updated to reflect changes in the Protocol or applicable regulations. Changes will be published in the official project repository.

s10.title: Contact
s10.body: For inquiries related to this Policy, contact us through the official project channels or at contact@ethernal.fund.

s1.title: Acceptance of Terms
s1.body: By interacting with the FondoRetiro DeFi smart contracts, including PersonalFundFactory, PersonalFund, Treasury, UserPreferences, and ProtocolRegistry, the user fully and unconditionally accepts these Terms and Conditions of Use.

s2.title: Protocol Description
s2.b1: Creation of personal retirement funds through PersonalFundFactory.
s2.b2: Deposit and withdrawal of USDC or other stable assets configured by the administrator.
s2.b3: Automatic or manual routing of deposits to registered DeFi protocols.
s2.b4: Management of user preferences and investment strategies via UserPreferences.
s2.b6: Application of configurable lock-up periods (timelock) between 1 and 40 years.

s3.title: Eligibility Requirements
s3.b1: Be between 18 and 70 years of declared age.
s3.b2: Declare a minimum retirement age of 60 years.
s3.b3: Provide initial capital within the configured minimum and maximum range.
s3.b4: Commit to a configured minimum monthly deposit.
s3.b5: Select an active and approved investment protocol in the ProtocolRegistry.
s3.b6: Not have a previously active fund (a user may hold only one active fund simultaneously).

s4.title: Nature of Smart Contracts
s4.b1: Smart contracts execute rules autonomously, deterministically, and immutably once deployed.
s4.b2: No human intermediary can reverse, cancel, or modify already confirmed transactions.
s4.b3: Contracts may contain errors or vulnerabilities. Use implies assuming this risk.
s4.b4: Interaction requires payment of gas fees, the cost of which varies and is the sole responsibility of the user.

s5.title: Timelock Period and Withdrawal
s5.b1: Funds will be locked during the timelock period selected when creating the fund (1 to 40 years).
s5.b2: During the timelock, it is not possible to withdraw funds except under emergency conditions provided for in the contract.
s5.b3: Upon expiration of the timelock, the user may withdraw according to the configured distribution rules.
s5.b4: The Protocol does not guarantee any returns. Rates are estimates from the underlying DeFi protocols.

s6.title: Administrator Role
s6.b1: Configuration of system parameters (capital ranges, fees, enabled protocols).
s6.b2: Authorization and revocation of contracts in UserPreferences.
s6.b4: Recovery of tokens sent by mistake (recoverTokens function).

s7.title: Associated Risks
s7.b1: Smart contract risk: errors, exploits, or vulnerabilities in the code.
s7.b2: DeFi protocol risk: third-party protocols may suffer failures or hacks.
s7.b3: Regulatory risk: applicable regulations may change and affect the legality of use.
s7.b4: Custody risk: loss of the private key implies permanent loss of access.
s7.b5: Liquidity risk: during the timelock, funds are not liquid.
s7.b6: Market risk: the value of stable assets may be affected by extreme conditions.
s7.b7: Network risk: congestion, forks, or interruptions may affect transaction execution.

s8.title: Limitation of Liability
s8.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, the Protocol, its developers, contributors, and administrator shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, or punitive damages resulting from the use or inability to use the Protocol.

s9.title: Intellectual Property
s9.body: The source code of the smart contracts is available in the official repository under the published license. The user may audit and study the code in accordance with the terms of said license.

s10.title: Modifications to the Protocol
s10.body: The Terms and the Protocol may be updated. New versions will take effect from their publication in the official repository. Continued use implies acceptance of the new terms.

s11.title: Applicable Law
s11.body: These Terms are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where the Protocol has its development headquarters. Any dispute shall be submitted to the competent courts of said jurisdiction.

s1.title: Nature of the Project
s1.body: FondoRetiro DeFi is a decentralized financial infrastructure (DeFi) project based on smart contracts on a public blockchain. It is NOT a regulated financial entity, bank, insurer, or state-guaranteed fund. Current versions include simulated contracts (Mock) for test environments that do NOT generate real returns.

s2.title: Does Not Constitute Financial Advice
s2.body: No content, functionality, projection, or calculation of the Protocol constitutes financial, investment, legal, tax, or any other professional advice. Consult qualified advisors before making any investment decision based on the Protocol.

s3.title: Risks of Total Loss of Funds
s3.b1: Vulnerabilities, bugs, or exploits in smart contracts of this Protocol or the underlying ones.
s3.b2: Reentrancy attacks, oracle manipulation, flash loan attacks, or other DeFi vectors.
s3.b3: Loss or compromise of the private key associated with the user's wallet.
s3.b4: Forks, 51% attacks, or other disruptions to the underlying blockchain network.
s3.b5: Loss of value of USDC or other stablecoins in the event of depeg.
s3.b6: Regulatory changes that prevent access to or use of the Protocol.
s3.b7: Failures or insolvency of integrated third-party DeFi protocols.

s4.title: No Performance Guarantee
s4.body: The Protocol does not guarantee any returns, interest rates, or capital preservation. Returns shown are estimates based on mock contracts and do not represent contractual commitments. In production, returns will depend exclusively on the performance of the selected DeFi protocols.

s5.title: User Responsibility
s5.b1: Custody and security of their private key and wallet.
s5.b2: Verification of contract addresses they interact with.
s5.b3: Understanding of configured parameters and their financial implications.
s5.b4: Compliance with tax obligations under the laws of their jurisdiction.
s5.b5: Verification of the regulatory status of DeFi protocol use in their country.
s5.b6: Correct approval (approve) of USDC before making deposits.

s6.title: No Deposit Insurance
s6.body: Deposited funds are not covered by any deposit insurance system, state guarantee, or equivalent mechanism. In the event of loss of funds, the user shall have no right to claim before any protection body.

s7.title: Use in Restricted Jurisdictions
s7.body: The Protocol may not be available or may be illegal in certain jurisdictions. The user is solely responsible for verifying whether its use is permitted in their country or region of residence.

s9.title: General Disclaimer
s9.body: TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, THE PROTOCOL, ITS DEVELOPERS, CONTRIBUTORS, AUDITORS, AND ADMINISTRATOR DISCLAIM ALL LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES, LOSSES, OR HARM ARISING FROM THE USE OR INABILITY TO USE THE PROTOCOL. USE IS AT THE USER'S SOLE RISK.

ourStory.metaDescription: Learn how a conversation with a child on the streets of Buenos Aires sparked the creation of Ethernal Fund — a decentralized retirement platform.
ourStory.fullStory: It all started one afternoon while our founder, Cristian F. Taborda, was picking up his children from school. Encountering a demonstration by retirees at the corner of Rodríguez Peña and Avenida Rivadavia, an innocent question from his son revealed a painful reality: the pension system had failed several generations of his own family. That moment awakened in him a profound determination: to create a real and sustainable alternative. Thus was born the idea of a decentralized application where every person can calculate, create, and manage their own retirement fund — with dignity and freedom.

definitions.title: Definitions
items: "Ethernal Fund" or "the Issuer": The decentralized personal retirement savings protocol built on the Arbitrum network, developed and maintained by the founding team led by Cristian F. Taborda.
"ETRF": The native utility token of the Ethernal Fund protocol, implemented as a smart contract on the Arbitrum network.
"Token Sale" or "Seed Round": The primary token sale event for ETRF tokens described in this document, corresponding to the first funding round of the protocol.
"Participant": Any natural or legal person who acquires ETRF tokens through the official smart contract during the Token Sale period.
"Vesting": The mechanism of gradual and linear release of ETRF tokens over a defined period, once the cliff period has elapsed.
"Cliff": The initial total token lock-up period, during which the Participant cannot claim any fraction of their purchased tokens.
"USDC": The USD Coin stablecoin issued by Circle Financial, LLC — the sole accepted means of payment in this Token Sale.

nature.title: Nature of the ETRF Token
items: ETRF is a utility token designed exclusively for use within the Ethernal Fund protocol ecosystem. Its primary function is to grant access to protocol features, including governance participation, access to premium features, and use as an internal unit of account.
THE ACQUISITION OF ETRF TOKENS DOES NOT CONSTITUTE: an investment in securities, shares, bonds, or any regulated financial instrument.
It is NOT a participation in the Issuer's profits, dividends, or cash flows.
It is NOT a right of ownership, voting, or control over Ethernal Fund.
It is NOT a promise or guarantee of economic return, value appreciation, or future liquidity.
The final classification of ETRF as a utility token or security will depend on the Participant's jurisdiction and applicable regulatory interpretation.

conditions.title: Participation Conditions
items: Be at least 18 years of age or the legal age of majority in your jurisdiction of residence.
Not reside or be located in any excluded jurisdiction (United States, China, North Korea, Iran, Cuba, Syria, Venezuela, and any country subject to comprehensive OFAC sanctions).

seedRound.title: Token Sale Conditions — Seed Round
items: Available tokens: 100,000,000 ETRF (one hundred million tokens).
Price per token: USD 0.01 payable in USDC on the Arbitrum network.
Hard Cap and per-wallet cap: maximum amounts defined in the Smart Contract at deployment.
Accepted payment: USDC exclusively.
Cliff and vesting: per immutable parameters defined in the Smart Contract at deployment.
During the cliff period, no tokens can be claimed. After the cliff, tokens are released linearly over the vesting period. The schedule runs from the time of each individual Participant's purchase.
Unclaimed tokens do not expire and remain available in the contract.

irreversibility.title: Transaction Irreversibility
irreversibility.body: All transactions executed on the Arbitrum blockchain are irreversible. Once USDC has been transferred to the Smart Contract, there is no refund, reversal, or cancellation mechanism. The Issuer does not have the technical capacity to reverse on-chain transactions.

risks.title: Risk Factors
items: Total Loss of Capital: the value of ETRF tokens may fall to zero. The Participant must have the economic capacity to absorb the total loss of the invested amount.
Smart Contract Risk: no audit guarantees the absence of bugs. An exploit could result in partial or total loss of funds.
Regulatory Risk: the regulatory framework for crypto assets is uncertain and constantly changing.
Liquidity Risk: there is no guarantee that ETRF tokens will be listed on any exchange or that a secondary market with sufficient liquidity will exist.
Technology Risk: the protocol depends on the Arbitrum and Ethereum networks. Failures or attacks on these networks could affect protocol availability.
Project Risk: the team may fail to execute the roadmap for technical, financial, regulatory, or personal reasons.
Custody Risk: tokens are held in the Participant's wallet. The Issuer has no access to private keys. Loss of wallet access means permanent loss of tokens.

executiveSummary.title: Executive Summary
executiveSummary.body: Ethernal Fund Protocol is a decentralized personal retirement fund system built on blockchain (Arbitrum / Polygon), enabling anyone in the world to create and manage their own retirement fund autonomously, transparently, and without traditional financial intermediaries. The protocol combines smart contracts written in Vyper with integrations to established DeFi protocols (Aave v3) and tokenized real-world assets (Ondo USDY / US T-Bills) to offer secure yields on USDC deposits.

problemSolution.title: Problem and Solution
items: Traditional pension systems face a structural crisis: growing deficits, inflation eroding purchasing power, and increasing labor informality. In Latin America, less than 40% of workers actively contribute to formal pension systems.
Conventional savings instruments present significant barriers: high minimums, opaque fees, dependence on intermediaries, and geographically restricted access.

Ethernal Fund Protocol resolves these limitations through smart contracts that allow each user to create their own personal retirement fund on blockchain, with customized parameters and without ceding control of their assets to any third party.
The protocol leverages DeFi to offer non-custodial, transparent, borderless, programmable, and composable financial instruments for long-term savings.

architecture.title: Protocol Architecture
items: PersonalFund.vy — The central contract. Each user has their own deployed instance (minimal proxy EIP-1167). Manages the complete fund lifecycle.
PersonalFundFactory.vy — Deploys new PersonalFund instances using the minimal proxy pattern (EIP-1167 / clones), significantly reducing gas costs.
Treasury.vy — Manages protocol fee collection (default 5%, maximum 10%) and acts as arbiter for early withdrawal requests.
ProtocolRegistry.vy — Curated catalog of DeFi protocols available for investment, with metadata: name, category, estimated APY, risk level, TVL, and verification status.
AaveV3Adapter.vy — Bridge to the Aave v3 lending market on Arbitrum One.
OndoUSDYAdapter.vy — Adapter for investing in USDY, a tokenized promissory note backed by short-term US Treasury bills (historical APY: 4.5%–5.5%).

lifecycle.title: Personal Fund Lifecycle
items: Fund Creation: user sets principal (0–100,000 USDC), monthly deposit, current age, retirement age, desired monthly income, and timelock years (15–50).
Accumulation Phase: user makes periodic monthly deposits and accumulates yield from DeFi protocols during the lockup period.
Early Withdrawal: requires approval from the protocol Treasury via requestEarlyRetirement(). The admin can approve or reject the request.
Emergency Withdrawal: the admin can announce an emergency with a mandatory 48-hour waiting period before the user can execute emergencyWithdraw().
Retirement Phase: upon timelock completion, the owner activates retirement() and the system automatically configures monthly auto-withdrawals.

tokenomics.title: ETRF Token — Tokenomics
items: ETRF is exclusively a utility token. It does NOT represent equity, debt, dividends, or any expectation of profit. Total supply: 1,000,000,000 ETRF (fixed, non-mintable post-deploy).
Premium Mode: users holding a minimum of ETRF unlock advanced features (reports, investment strategies, alerts). The token is only verified, not consumed.
Fee Discount: users can pay management fees in ETRF instead of USDC, receiving a discount. ETRF tokens used are burned, reducing circulating supply.
Public Sale: 30% (300,000,000) — distributed via SaleETRF → VestingETRF.
Team: 20% (200,000,000) — 1-year cliff + 25% unlock + 75% linear over 3 years.
Ecosystem: 20% (200,000,000) — incentives, partnerships, integrations.

security.title: Security and Risk Management
items: All core contracts are written in Vyper, which prohibits multiple inheritance, operator overloading, recursion, and inline modifiers — significantly reducing attack surface.
Smart contract risk: no code is 100% bug-free. Funds may be lost in the event of an exploit.
DeFi protocol risk: Aave v3 and Ondo USDY are external protocols. An exploit there could affect deposited funds.
Stablecoin depeg risk: USDC may lose its USD parity under extreme circumstances.
Regulatory risk: the legal framework for digital assets is uncertain and varies by jurisdiction.
Admin risk: dependence on the Ethernal Foundation for key administrative operations while the protocol is not fully decentralized.

legal.title: Legal and Regulatory Framework
items: Core contracts (PersonalFund, Factory, Treasury, adapters) are licensed under BUSL-1.1 until 2030-12-31, then migrate to GPL-2.0+.
Infrastructure and token contracts (ProtocolRegistry, UserPreferences, ETRF, SaleETRF, VestingETRF) are licensed under Apache-2.0 or MIT perpetually.
The protocol operates in a non-custodial manner and does not require user identification at the smart contract level.
The timelock mechanism (15–50 years) incorporates an anti-money-laundering compliance property by architectural design ("friction by design").

roadmap.title: Roadmap
items: Q2 2026 — Testnet: Full deployment on Arbitrum Sepolia. Security audit. Bug bounty program.
Q3 2026 — Mainnet v1: Launch on Arbitrum One. ETRF public sale (Seed Round). First user funds.
Q4 2026 — Expansion: Integration of new DeFi protocols. Deployment on Polygon. More RWA adapters.
2027 — Decentralization: On-chain governance for Protocol Registry. Reduction of admin privileges.
2030-12-31 — Open Source: Migration from BUSL-1.1 to GPL-2.0+ licenses. Fully open-source protocol.

risk.title: Risk Disclosure
risk.subtitle: Before using Ethernal Fund, read and understand these risks. They are written in plain language so you can make an informed decision.
risk.criticalWarning: This protocol is not regulated or supervised by any financial authority. There is no guarantee of fund recovery. It is not a bank, not a regulated investment fund, and is not covered by any deposit insurance. ONLY USE FUNDS WHOSE TOTAL LOSS YOU CAN AFFORD.

guaranteed.title: What IS guaranteed by the protocol's design
items: Funds always return to the fund owner — never to third parties.
The admin cannot transfer your funds to any wallet other than yours.
Any emergency withdrawal has a 48-hour waiting period, during which you can cancel it.
The maximum fee is fixed in the contract and cannot exceed 10%, regardless of what the Foundation decides.
The code is public and verifiable on the blockchain by anyone.

questions.title: Before you continue, ask yourself:
items: Do you understand that you can lose 100% of the deposited funds?
Are you depositing money that you won't need for 15 years or more?
Do you understand that blockchain transactions are irreversible?
Do you know what a smart contract is and what its risks are?
Have you consulted with a financial or legal advisor if you have doubts?
questions.footer: If you answered "no" to any of these questions, we recommend taking more time before depositing funds. You can read the technical Whitepaper or contact us at contact@ethernal.fund.

risks.title: You can lose everything you deposit
risks.summary: Funds deposited in the protocol can be lost in their entirety.
risks.detail: Ethernal Fund operates on blockchain smart contracts. If there is a bug, security vulnerability, or exploit in the code — even after being audited — funds can be irreversibly lost. There is no insurance, state guarantee, or recovery mechanism. Before depositing, make sure you understand that you are fully assuming that risk.

risks.title: Transactions are irreversible
risks.summary: Once you send USDC to the protocol, there is no possible refund.
risks.detail: Blockchain operations are permanent. The protocol does not have the technical capacity to reverse transactions, return funds by mistake, or process refunds. If you send funds to the wrong address, use the wrong network, or make any error in the transaction, those funds will be permanently lost.

risks.title: Your funds will be locked for years
risks.summary: The timelock is a minimum of 15 years. You cannot withdraw early without protocol approval.
risks.detail: When creating a retirement fund, you choose a lock-up period between 15 and 50 years. During that time, you cannot withdraw your funds under any circumstances without requesting and receiving explicit approval from the Ethernal Foundation. The protocol may reject the request. Think of this as a very long-term commitment: it is not for funds you might need in the coming years.

risks.title: Integrated DeFi protocols also have risks
risks.summary: Aave v3 and Ondo USDY are external protocols. A problem in them also affects you.
risks.detail: Ethernal invests your funds in protocols like Aave v3 (lending) and Ondo USDY (tokenized Treasury bonds). These are external protocols with their own risks: exploits, emergency pauses, governance changes, or liquidity issues. An incident in any of those protocols could reduce or eliminate your balance, regardless of Ethernal's correct operation.

risks.title: USDC can lose its value
risks.summary: USDC is a stablecoin, but it is not guaranteed 1:1 with the dollar at all times.
risks.detail: Although USDC is designed to maintain parity with the US dollar, risk scenarios exist: liquidity issues at Circle (the issuer), regulatory changes affecting reserves, or systemic market events. In March 2023, USDC temporarily lost its parity. Your balance in the protocol is denominated in USDC, so any depegging directly affects you.

risks.title: The regulatory framework may change
risks.summary: Rules for crypto assets in LATAM and the world are constantly evolving.
risks.detail: Regulators in Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, and other countries are developing legal frameworks for digital assets. Regulatory changes could affect your ability to use the protocol, the tax classification of your returns, or the protocol's operation in your country. The protocol may need to modify or restrict its operation due to new legal requirements.

risks.title: The protocol admin has limited powers over your fund
risks.summary: The Ethernal Foundation can intervene in emergency situations.
risks.detail: Although Ethernal Fund is a non-custodial protocol, the Foundation maintains an administrator role with specific capabilities: it can approve or reject early withdrawal requests, announce emergencies with a 48-hour waiting period, and manage which DeFi protocols are available. These functions exist for security and regulatory compliance reasons. However, funds always return to the owner — the admin cannot transfer them to third parties.
